source: CelesTrak GP (OMM) snapshot, element epochs up to 2026-10-30 22:52 UTC; groups active, fengyun-1c/cosmos-2251/iridium-33 debris + name searches DEB, R/B, COSMOS, OBJECT, OPS, METEOR. Data: CelesTrak (celestrak.org)
method: SGP4 (python-sgp4 SatrecArray, 52 CPU procs) on a 10 s grid; GPU sorted-grid spatial hash (cell 86 km) per step on Tesla PG503-216; linear-relative-motion TCA refinement; threshold 5 km
pc_note: log10_pc_max = max Pc (no covariance in public TLEs): worst case over an isotropic Gaussian of unknown size in the encounter plane, HBR from SATCAT RCS (equivalent-circle radius, both objects summed). SGP4/TLE errors are ~1 km or more; this is a screening view, not an operational Pc.

summary.top_list: closest encounter per pair, 200 pairs with rel speed >= 0.1 km/s, sorted by min range

validation.notes: socrates_overlap = fraction of the listed top pairs matched to a SOCRATES event (same pair, |dTCA|<=60 s). SOCRATES lists only payload-involved pairs, so debris-on-debris events cannot match. SOCRATES used older element sets (its run started at the window it reports) than our snapshot, and both use the same public SGP4 data, so agreement checks the screening, not truth.
